bindings.explanation: REQ-6-1 states that any valid Request changes review blocks merging, so a PR whose only unmet condition is such a review must not offer an actionable merge control (REQ-6-5 requires a visibly disabled Merge pull request button plus the unmet condition). Fixture: the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 authors as alice-dev and targets protected main (both Require 1 approval and Require status check test enabled), with compare commit c-acme-3. bob-reviewer's seeded non-author approval for c-acme-3 is still valid, the fixture replaces the seeded pending check with 'success' for that same commit, and dana-dev (an existing organization member given the minimal Write grant needed to be an eligible reviewer, not the PR author) has a non-stale Changes requested decision on c-acme-3. So every other rule is satisfied and only the blocking review remains. APP.pullSidebar, the real merge-area renderer, derives the merge control from the approval count alone and therefore renders an enabled Merge pull request control (data-action="merge-pr") although a valid Request changes review blocks the merge; the in-check control (same fixture with the blocking review removed, which must be mergeable) shows the fixture itself is otherwise valid. Correction from the failed run: the subject is bound as the exact namespace member APP.pullSidebar with kind "function" (the earlier kind "method" produced "found 0") and it is invoked through the actual source object so the real renderer runs.

bindings.requirement_text:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. A “branch protection rule” is a persistent merge restriction bound to one exact branch name, displayed in the frontend under Settings → Branches, with the backend storing the branch name and rule toggles. This product supports only two independently selectable requirements: “at least 1 valid Approve from someone other than the PR author” and “required check `test` is success”. For a given reviewer on the same current compare commit, only the reviewer's latest decision among Comment, Approve, and Request changes counts. The PR author cannot satisfy the approval requirement; any valid Request changes blocks merging; when the compare branch gains a new commit, all decisions become stale and a new review is required. “Checks” is the results area on the PR detail page attached to the current compare commit; the `test` status of pending, success, or failure, together with the setter and time, must be stored, and only a repository Admin may update that status from this area. The system blocks direct writes to a protected branch and applies the rule during subsequent PR merging. The repository provides a Settings link followed by a Branches link. The rule form opens from the Add branch protection rule button and contains a field labeled Branch name pattern (an exact branch name, with no wildcard semantics), checkboxes named Require 1 approval and Require status check test, and a Create button; an existing rule uses Save changes. After saving and reloading, the branch name is visible verbatim with the summaries 1 approval and Require status check test. For a non-Admin, Add branch protection rule is absent, even if Settings or Branches remain accessible; rejecting a save alone is insufficient. On the PR detail page, the Checks area is available on arrival, displays test: pending initially, and offers the Admin a combobox named test status with a clickable option named success and a Save button. Saving displays test: success and identifies the setter and time, and reloading preserves the result for that compare commit. Seed data comprises a repository Admin and a readable non-Admin account, a dedicated repository and exact branch name with no existing rule before creation, and a separate Open PR targeting protected main with its current test check initially pending.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-branch-protection.png)

bindings.explanation: REQ-6-5 requires each enabled protection rule to be enforced independently when the target branch is protected, so with Require status check test enabled and the required test check of the current compare commit not success, the PR must stay blocked and keep only a non-actionable merge control with an explanation. Fixture uses only restored seed state: the Open PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main (both rules on), bob-reviewer's valid non-author approval for compare commit c-acme-3 satisfies the approval rule, no valid Request changes exists, and the seeded check record for p-1 at c-acme-3 is 'pending', i.e. not success. APP.pullSidebar, the real merge-area renderer, never reads the check rule when computing eligibility, so it renders an enabled Merge pull request control (data-action="merge-pr") for a PR that the status-check rule must block. bindings.requirement_text: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
